q.en: Why were the Sergeant Rotten Teeth books pulled from the library?
q.zh: 《腐牙中士》系列为什么被撤下图书馆书架？

options.en: They were stolen.
They were too old.
A parent complained about the series, so the librarian removed them for review.
options.zh: 有家长投诉该系列，于是图书管理员将其撤下以待审查。

options.en: They were destroyed in a fire that burned the whole library down one weekend when no one was there, and only the cookbooks were saved
options.zh: 它们在一场大火中被毁，整座图书馆烧光，偏偏只救出了烹饪书

explain.en: Mrs. McGuinness says "We had a parent complain about the series, so I pulled the books until they can be looked at more closely."
explain.zh: 麦吉尼斯女士说：“有家长投诉了这个系列，所以我把书撤下来，等仔细审查。”

q.en: What did author Dan Eaton say his books were meant to do?
q.zh: 作者丹·伊顿说他的书 intended 是为了什么？

options.en: Encourage tooth care in a fun way.
options.zh: 以有趣的方式鼓励爱护牙齿。

options.en: Teach kids to be mean to their friends at the dentist
options.zh: 教孩子们在看牙医时对自己的朋友使坏

options.en: Sell toys.
Scare children.

explain.en: Dan Eaton's email: "I wanted to encourage tooth care in a fun way."
explain.zh: 丹·伊顿的邮件写道：“我想以有趣的方式鼓励大家爱护牙齿。”

options.en: A school subject that students must pass every single year to move up to the next grade in school
options.zh: 一门学生每年都必须及格才能升入下一年级学校课程的科目

options.en: A group of people who consider or decide on a course of action.
options.zh: 考虑或决定某项行动方案的一群人。

options.en: A newspaper.
A type of book.

explain.en: Glossary: "committee (n.) a group of people who consider or decide on a course of action."
explain.zh: 词汇表：“committee——考虑或决定某项行动方案的一群人。”

q.en: What does the First Amendment protect in this story?
q.zh: 在这个故事中，第一修正案保护什么？

options.en: The right to build bombs.
Freedom of speech, which includes the right to have books in a library.
options.zh: 言论自由，书中说它包括在图书馆拥有书籍的权利。

options.en: The right to ban all books that any parent happens not to like, even ones about science, history, animals, and counting
options.zh: 禁掉任何家长碰巧不喜欢的书的权力，连讲科学、历史、动物和数数的书也包括

options.en: Freedom to never read.

explain.en: "The First Amendment gives Americans several freedoms, including freedom of speech. The courts consider books a type of speech."
explain.zh: 书中说“第一修正案赋予美国人若干自由，包括言论自由。法庭把书籍视为一种言论。”

q.en: What does Noni learn about freedom of speech?
q.zh: 诺妮学到了关于言论自由的什么？

options.en: That books should always be banned.
That speech has no limits.
That it gives people the chance to think, question, and decide for themselves, and is strongest in a library.
options.zh: 它让人们有机会自己思考、质疑和决定，并在图书馆里最为有力。

options.en: That only adults have free speech, because children are too young to have opinions worth protecting and should only listen to grown-ups, who decide what they may read
options.zh: 只有成年人有言论自由，因为孩子太小、不配有值得保护的看法，只能听大人的，由大人决定他们能读什么

explain.en: Noni reads Dan's email: "we have... the chance to think, question, and decide issues for ourselves" and Mrs. McGuinness says "freedom-of-speech rights are strongest" in the library.
explain.zh: 诺妮读到丹的邮件：“我们拥有……自己思考、质疑和决定的机会”，麦吉尼斯女士也说在图书馆里“言论自由权利最为有力”。

q.en: Why does Mrs. McGuinness say a book on building bombs could be banned more easily?
q.zh: 麦吉尼斯女士为什么说一本教造炸弹的书更容易被禁？

options.en: Because it is long.
Because it is unpopular and no child has ever asked to read it, so the library took it off the shelf for good and sold the copies
options.zh: 因为它不受欢迎，从没孩子要求读它，于是图书馆干脆把它下架并卖掉了存书

options.en: Because kids like it.
Because it presents a clear danger, unlike the Sergeant Rotten Teeth books.
options.zh: 因为它构成明显危险，而不像《腐牙中士》那些书。

explain.en: "That probably wouldn't need a big review process to ban, because it presents a clear danger."
explain.zh: 书中说“那大概不需要大费周章的审查程序就能禁掉，因为它构成明显的危险。”

q.en: What was the final vote of the book review committee?
q.zh: 图书审查委员会的最终投票结果是什么？

options.en: 3-2 to return the books to the library shelf.
5-0 to ban them, with every committee member voting against the books
options.zh: 5比0，委员会每位成员都投票反对这些书

options.en: 2-3 to ban them.
A tie.

explain.en: "On a vote of 3-2, the book review committee decided Monday to return the books to the library shelf."
explain.zh: 书中说“周一，图书审查委员会以3比2的投票决定将书放回图书馆书架。”

q.en: How does the author present both sides of the book-ban argument?
q.zh: 作者如何呈现禁书争议的双方观点？

options.en: By ignoring the issue.
By banning the books.
By only showing one side, the author who agreed with the ban wrote the whole school paper, let no one reply, and tore out every page that disagreed with her
options.zh: 只展示一方观点：赞同禁书的作者写了整份校刊，不让任何人反驳，还撕掉了所有持不同意见的版面

options.en: By having Ashley write a column supporting the ban and Miguel write one opposing it in the school paper.
options.zh: 让阿什莉在校刊写支持禁书的专栏，米格尔写反对的专栏。

explain.en: "I had coeditor Ashley write a column in support of the ban and coeditor Miguel write a column opposed to it."
explain.zh: 书中说“我让联合编辑阿什莉写一篇支持禁书的专栏，联合编辑米格尔写一篇反对的专栏。”

q.en: What role did Noni take on at the end?
q.zh: 结尾时诺妮承担了什么角色？

options.en: She left the school.
She served on the book review committee and cast the decisive vote.
options.zh: 她加入了图书审查委员会，并投下了决定性的一票。

options.en: She became librarian.
She wrote the banned books herself under a secret pen name that no one in the school could ever guess, find, or prove
options.zh: 她用没人能猜到、找到或证实的笔名亲自写了那些被禁的书

explain.en: Mrs. McGuinness wanted "a student to serve on the committee: me," and "Student Noni Lopez cast the decisive vote."
explain.zh: 麦吉尼斯女士希望“有一名学生加入委员会：我”，而“学生诺妮·洛佩兹投下了决定性的一票。”

q.en: What is the author's main message?
q.zh: 作者的主要信息是什么？

options.en: That free speech and the chance to think for oneself matter, even when people disagree about a book.
options.zh: 即使人们对一本书有分歧，言论自由和独立思考的机会依然重要。

options.en: That protests never work.
That librarians are unfair.
That all books should be banned, even picture books, the dictionary, the menu at the school lunch table, the signs in the hallway, and the calendars on the wall
options.zh: 所有书都应该被禁，连图画书、字典、学校午餐桌上的菜单、走廊里的标语和墙上的日历都不例外

explain.en: The book's Focus Question is "What does Noni learn about freedom of speech?" and the story shows the value of the First Amendment and open discussion.
explain.zh: 本书焦点问题是“诺妮学到了关于言论自由的什么？”，故事展现了第一修正案和公开讨论的价值。

prompt.en: Write a letter to Mrs. McGuinness stating your position on whether the Sergeant Rotten Teeth series should be banned from the school library, and explain your reasons using the idea of freedom of speech.
prompt.zh: 给麦吉尼斯女士写一封信，说明你认为《腐牙中士》系列是否应该从学校图书馆禁掉，并运用言论自由的理念解释你的理由。

en: State your position clearly—either keep the books or ban them.
Use evidence from the book, such as Dan Eaton's email about the First Amendment and the chance to think for oneself.
zh: 清楚地表明你的立场——保留这些书或禁掉它们。
运用书中的证据，例如丹·伊顿关于第一修正案以及“自己思考机会”的邮件。
